payload.name: Preserve Existing Explicit Facts During Memory Merge
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory with new evidence, use this to retain all explicit claims from the prior version unless directly contradicted.
content: During CRUD-stage UPDATE/MERGE, compare the existing memory's explicit facts with the new evidence before changing content.

Keep every explicit claim from the existing version (including specific passions, stated beliefs, and named effects) unless the new evidence directly contradicts it; express both old and new facts in the merged memory.

Do not reduce a specific claim to a broader category (for example, do not turn 'passion for fantasy stuff' into 'enjoys fantasy genres') and do not let a newly mentioned theme replace the memory's previous focus.

If the new evidence concerns a different domain, preserve the current memory in place and create or update a separate memory for the new domain; change only fields the new evidence actually contradicts.
Preserve the original world_start unless the new evidence explicitly indicates a new start; stop after merging explicit facts and do not infer additional relationships.

solves: Later messages often introduce a related but different topic, and an update/merge can rewrite a precise memory into a broader summary, dropping exact claims (like a specific passion or its stated effect) that future questions rely on. This skill makes update/merge operations combine new evidence with the existing memory's explicit facts instead of replacing them.
